title: Orunmila mark (raw observation), schema version 1: DRAFT
description: Every source's output is turned into marks of this one shape by its adapter, and intake appends them to the session's raw log (JSON Lines, one mark per line, never edited). Sources never write to the log themselves.
$comment: brief v3 lines 209-268. Draft from Phase 1 slice A1: nothing writes or reads this format yet. Unknown fields are allowed, because the brief lets v1 add fields without a version bump (line 209); a reader must ignore what it does not know. Rules the brief states but a schema cannot hold (seq strictly increasing, the hash chain, redaction before hashing) are checked elsewhere (A3a, A4, A5, A6).

schema_version.description: All carry a `schema_version`. Once v1 ships, fields may be added but never renamed or removed without a version bump.

session_id.description: The session the mark belongs to. A sub-agent's work belongs to its session.
session_id.$comment: brief v3 lines 218, 256 (the example's field; its format is not set by the brief)

seq.description: One counter per session, assigned by the Opon's intake, strictly increasing. This is the true order of arrival.
seq.$comment: brief v3 line 237. Marks start at 1; 0 is the session header (agent's choice, LD10).

source.description: One of `agent_claim`, `hook`, `sentinel`, `git`, `process`, `law_gate`. New sources are added to this list by contract change.

agent.description: The agent whose session this is, for example `claude-code`; null when the source cannot know it.
agent.$comment: brief v3 line 221 (the example's field; null allowed is the agent's choice, LD11)

turn.description: Every Glove mark, and every law-gate mark, names the agent's turn. Sources that know nothing of turns (sentinel, git, process) write `null`. The session's end belongs to no turn, so its mark writes `null` too.
turn.$comment: brief v3 line 255; the session end's null is the agent's choice, LD55 (format change approved by O 2026-11-17). Its type is set by the turn rules, allOf/0 to /2, which cover every source (LD87).

sub_agent.description: `{ "id": ..., "type": ... }` when the action happened inside a sub-agent, otherwise `null`.

observed_at.description: `observed_at` is wall-clock time for humans only.
observed_at.$comment: brief v3 line 238. UTC ISO 8601 with a Z, as the example (line 224); the exact pattern is the agent's choice, LD12.

mono_ns.description: The system-wide monotonic clock (never goes backwards), stamped as close to the moment of observation as the source allows; if a source cannot stamp it, intake stamps arrival time and records that in `detail.stamped_by`. Use it for all timing maths.
mono_ns.$comment: brief v3 line 238; brief v4 line 238: written as a decimal string of the integer, because a JSON number is exact only up to 2^53 (about 104 days of nanoseconds since boot); compared as a big integer (open point P1, decided 2026-11-16).

target.description: What the mark is about. `target.kind`: `file`, `dir`, `command`, `process`, `claim`, `turn`, `tool`, `network`, or `session`.
target.$comment: brief v3 lines 244, 259; `session` is the agent's choice, LD55

says.description: A fixed verb list: created, modified, deleted, renamed, started, exited, ended (a turn finished, a tool call failed, or the session ended), prompted (a user prompt arrived), read, contacted, called, claimed, checked (the law gate checked a turn), fingerprinted (the Opon recorded a file's fingerprint), gap (a source lost or dropped events), tampered (source process: Orunmila's own logs, frozen configuration, code or the agent's hook settings changed during the session, or a payload arrived from a process other than the one pinned to the session). Also tick (heartbeat).
says.$comment: brief v3 line 245; brief v4 line 245 adds tampered (decision I-1, 2026-11-16); ended for the session is the agent's choice, LD55

detail.description: Named detail slots (the spec gives each a schema).

cause_hint.description: Filled by sources that know their cause, for example a hook mark carries the tool call id. Sentinel marks usually leave it null.

prev_hash.description: Each mark's hash covers its own content plus the previous mark's hash. The first mark's previous hash is the session header's.

hash.description: Content is serialised in one canonical form before hashing (RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization, or an equally exact rule written into the spec), so anyone can recompute the same hash.
hash.$comment: brief v3 line 247. The exact bytes hashed are slice A3a.

allOf.$comment: brief v3 line 255: Glove and law-gate marks name the turn, except the session's end (LD55)
agent's choice, LD55: only the agent's own hook ends a session, outside any turn
brief v3 line 255: sentinel, git and process write null
brief v3 line 253: agent_claim is the agent's closing claim
brief v3 lines 257, 265: the claim stays a claimed mark, with its text
brief v3 line 242: each check is a checked mark on the turn, with detail.result
brief v3 lines 242, 245: checked means the law gate checked a turn
brief v3 line 346: tick marks have source process
agent's choice, LD13: only tick and gap may have a null target
brief v3 line 341: a gap mark names what was lost
brief v3 line 257: each user prompt is a prompted mark on the turn, with the text in detail.prompt
brief v3 line 258: every tool call gives a started mark and one outcome mark, both with the tool call id in cause_hint and the tool's name in detail.tool
brief v3 line 258: every outcome mark carries detail.exit_status
brief v3 line 240: exited marks always carry detail.exit_status
brief v3 line 259: a command targets { kind: command, text }
brief v3 lines 245, 264: file changes, the Glove's edit outcomes and the sentinel's marks alike
brief v3 line 264: a created mark leaves fingerprint_before out
brief v3 lines 259, 261: a read targets the file, or the folder searched
brief v3 line 259: a network contact targets { kind: network, host, url }
brief v3 lines 259, 263: any other tool targets { kind: tool, name }; called carries tool_input
brief v4 line 245: a tampered mark has source process and says what was tampered with
brief v4 line 265: a renamed mark also carries from, the old path

hash.description: A chain hash: sha256 and 64 lowercase hex digits.
hash.$comment: brief v3 line 247; the prefix is the example's (lines 230-231)

fingerprint.description: A file or output fingerprint: plain SHA-256, or keyed HMAC-SHA-256 for files on the redaction list. null when unknown.
fingerprint.$comment: brief v3 lines 228, 249. The hmac-sha256 prefix is the agent's choice, LD14.

count.description: A line count; null unless both states are known.

instant.description: On a gap for intake's downtime: one end of the window. since is when intake last wrote before it stopped (the latest record among the sessions it was serving); until is when it ran again.
instant.$comment: agent's choice, B1c-2 (test 84); wording approved by O 2026-11-17

mono_ns.description: The monotonic clock at that moment, as a decimal string.

observed_at.description: Wall-clock time at that moment, for humans, and the only clock that compares across a reboot.

glove_tool_mark.$comment: A Glove (source hook) mark about one tool call: started, an outcome verb, or ended on something other than a turn (brief v3 line 258). It names no required keys: the root requires source, says and target (LD81, LD87).

session_target.$comment: A mark about the session itself: target { kind: session } (LD55).

kind.description: `file`, `dir`, `command`, `process`, `claim`, `turn`, `tool`, `network`, or `session` (the session itself, for its end).
kind.$comment: brief v3 line 244; `session` is the agent's choice, LD55

path.description: The file or folder. Normalise paths: convert to repo-relative, resolve symlinks, and normalise case on case-insensitive filesystems.
path.$comment: brief v3 lines 226, 339; brief v4 line 345: a path outside the project root is absolute, with outside: true. Normalisation is slice A7.

outside.description: A path outside the project root keeps its absolute real path, with `target.outside: true`.
outside.$comment: brief v4 line 345 (open point P2, decided 2026-11-16)

id.description: A turn, target `{ "kind": "turn", "id": ... }`. The session itself, `{ "kind": "session", "id": ... }`, with its session id.
id.$comment: brief v3 line 257; the session target is the agent's choice, LD55

name.description: Any other tool targets `{ "kind": "tool", "name": ... }`. A process target may name the process: `intake` for Orunmila's own intake.
name.$comment: brief v3 line 259; the process name is the agent's choice, LD56

host.description: A network contact targets `{ "kind": "network", "host": ..., "url": ... }`; for a web search `host` is `null`, because the agent's tool picks the hosts and Orunmila does not see them.

query.description: For a web search, the query goes in `query`.

tool.description: The tool's name, on both marks of a tool call; null when the source did not record it (today's write and read records name no tool).
tool.$comment: brief v3 lines 241, 258; null allowed is the agent's choice, LD33

exit_status.description: `pass`, `fail` or `unknown`. Every outcome mark carries it.

exit_code.description: Only when it is truly known. Never invent a code. (Claude Code reports pass or fail only; exit 3 arrives as fail.) Only a command's outcome carries it.

output_ref.description: When the output is longer, the fingerprint of the full output, which is kept beside the log.

vcs.description: Git state in a command's output, the agent's testimony: one entry for each record today's capture writes (a commit and branch, each pull request, each set of CI checks), with today's field names.
vcs.$comment: brief v3 line 267. Entry shapes are today's capture records, not restated here.

read_kind.description: `full` only when the adapter can show the tool returned the whole file, `range` when it returned only part, `pattern` when the agent only searched, `null` when the adapter cannot tell.

fingerprint.description: The file's fingerprint (for a read, of the whole file as it was when the hook ran; it does not prove what the agent saw).

fingerprint_before.description: `null` when the before-state is unknown; a `created` mark leaves the field out.

lines_added.description: Never counted against an assumed-empty file.

lines_removed.description: Never counted against an assumed-empty file.

diff_ref.description: The fingerprint of the diff, which is kept beside the log. Plain SHA-256 of the redacted copy.

no_diff.description: When there is no diff, says why: `binary`, or `too_large` (over the size limit recorded in the session header).

tool_input.description: What a called tool was given.

tool_result_excerpt.description: Only when the user switches result capture on.

tool_result_size.description: Only when the user switches result capture on.

claim_unconfirmed.description: On a claimed mark: true when the agent's host gave no final text for the turn, so the claim's text could not be confirmed as the turn's own and is empty (N10). Absent otherwise.
claim_unconfirmed.$comment: agent's choice, LD85: today's turn_claim field (docs/SCHEMA.md), which the A8 adapter already carries

findings.description: Each law the check found broken, with the quoted text it judged; empty when it passed or skipped.
findings.$comment: brief v3 line 242 ("with the law and the quoted text"), test 61 ("laws and quoted text"); the shape is the agent's choice, LD36

severity.description: block or warn, as the law set it.

quote.description: The sentence the law judged; null when the finding has none.

reason.description: Why a check was skipped, for example: could not confirm the current turn. On the session's end, the reason the agent gave; on the intake's closing note, why it stopped.
reason.$comment: brief v3 lines 242, 575; agent's choice of name, LD36; the session end's and the closing note's use, LD55 and LD56

lost.description: A gap mark names what was lost.
lost.$comment: brief v3 line 341; the field name is the agent's choice, LD15

stamped_by.description: If a source cannot stamp mono_ns, intake stamps arrival time and records that here.

what.description: On a tampered mark, what was tampered with: `hook_settings`, `frozen_config`, `log_location`, `orunmila_code` or `foreign_sender`.

channel.description: Glove marks: how the mark reached intake. `http` for HTTP hooks, whose sender intake pins to the session's process at first contact; `command` for a command hook, which the agent can forge until the separate-user setup (Phase 5).

from.description: On a renamed mark, the old path, normalised like `target.path`.
from.$comment: brief v4 line 265 (open point P3, decided 2026-11-16)

from_human.description: On a prompted mark: false for a prompt the agent's tool wrote itself (a task notification, a sub-agent hand-back), which does not refill the gate's block budget.

redactions.description: Noting the redaction: the kinds of secret replaced with [REDACTED:<kind>], never the values.
redactions.$comment: brief v3 line 248; a list of kinds is the agent's choice, LD15

since.$comment: agent's choice, B1c-2 (test 84); wording approved by O 2026-11-17

until.$comment: agent's choice, B1c-2 (test 84); wording approved by O 2026-11-17

sessions.description: On a gap for intake's downtime: every session intake was serving when it stopped, each of which gets this same gap.
sessions.$comment: brief v4 line 851 (test 84: naming the sessions active at its last tick); the name is the agent's choice, wording approved by O 2026-11-17

clock_reset.description: On a gap for intake's downtime: true when the machine's monotonic clock restarted meanwhile (a reboot), so since and until compare only by wall time. Absent otherwise.
clock_reset.$comment: agent's choice, B1c-2 (test 84); wording approved by O 2026-11-17

sender_pid.description: On a tampered mark for a foreign sender: the process that sent the payload. On the Glove mark that pinned the session (its first HTTP payload): the pinned process, so a restarted intake re-pins from the record. Only intake writes it.
sender_pid.$comment: brief v4 line 245 ("with the evidence"); the name is the agent's choice, B1b, wording approved by O 2026-11-17; the pinning mark's use, LD58 (approved by O 2026-11-17)

pinned_pid.description: On a tampered mark for a foreign sender: the process the session is pinned to, its first HTTP sender.
pinned_pid.$comment: brief v4 line 247; the name is the agent's choice, B1b, wording approved by O 2026-11-17

received.description: On a tampered mark for a foreign sender: the payload as it arrived, kept as text for evidence and redacted like any mark. It is never the session's own mark.
received.$comment: brief v4 line 245; the name is the agent's choice, B1b, wording approved by O 2026-11-17

allOf.$comment: brief v3 line 266: diffs stay out of the raw log
brief v3 line 266: no_diff only when there is no diff
brief v3 line 264: line counts are null unless both states are known
brief v3 line 261: pattern for a search
